properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/12/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/12/2022
Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 942383
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/12/2022
Comments: On January 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. At the time of inspection, contractors where excavating the area in front of the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the well pad. The depth of the excavation was about 4 to 5 ft. The area of the infiltration berm that had yet to be excavated had a conductivity greater than 4,000 uS/cm. The design of the trench along the west end of the pad caused production fluid to flow to the southwest corner also. The southwest area of the pad also has a drainage culvert with the outlet pipe draining to the infiltration berm. The pooled production fluid in the northwest infiltration berm has been vacuumed out. The conductivity of the soil in front of that infiltration berm was over 4,000 uS/cm. No excavation has been done to this area. The northwest plunge pool filled back with water. The conductivity of the water was over 4,000 uS/cm. A sample was collected from the plunge pool and will be analyzed for SAC code 942. Mr. Rodriguez thinks that the seal around the outlet pipe from the drainage culvert in that area is failing, resulting in water in the plunge pool. There were no new seeps or areas where the production fluid has appeared off the well pad edge. STL Resources plans to finish removing the impacted soil from the southwest infiltration berm and move to the northwest infiltration berm to begin removing impacted soil there. Mr. Rodriguez said that a vacuum truck was scheduled to vacuum out the water in the northwest plunge pool and the water that had drained into the culverts from the trench along the west end of the pad. The spill of production fluid off the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 401. Clean Streams Law 402(b) is being supplanted by Clean Streams Law 401. Violations from Inspection Report 3305227 remain outstanding.

Comments: On August 6, 2024, the Department of Oil and Gas inspector, Cody Murray, conducted an onsite inspection of the HERBERT C SMITH 193F (Permit # 021-20853), operated by VESSELS COAL GAS INC.. • There is no visible well posting and no well tag ID on the well anywhere to be found. MIA 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/03/2023 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Jones Twp, Elk county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/03/2023
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 993563
Permit API: 047-25052
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/03/2023
Comments: This is a complaint inspection following a report by the operator of a large production water spill at this site on 4/26 at 7:30 am. An initial site visit was performed by WQSS Rob Bechtel. This inspection was performed with Seneca's Jeff Passerello.The initial spill occurred when a cast iron gate valve failed as the operator was pumping production water to a stimulation operation on the E09-U pad. The pump was in operation at 50 barrels per minute. The operator was able to stop the leak eventually. Water spread out across the northern edge of the site, entering a perimeter ditch. It then ran around the edge ditch of the site and eventually entered an infiltration berm on the southwest corner of the location. The operator brought in a pump and was able to collect a significant amount of liquid from this location. The operator's estimate is that 1500+ barrels of produced water was released. The operator has scraped up ~150 tons of material from the surface of the location and staged it on site to remove to the landfill. A pump is placed and the operator is using it to pump water collecting in the berm into tanks on site. Water does not appear to have passed the berm at this time, at least superficially. The operator has brought in ARM Group to do an initial analysis of the site and to take samples for removal to the landfill. Further inspection on this site will be done as necessary as cleanup continues.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 2019-09-16
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 862274
Permit API: 123-26419
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-09-16
Comments: This inspection was performed in response to a report, by the Operator, of a small release of crude oil along Irvine Run, in Brokenstraw Township, Warren County, PA. This is the second release to have occurred in association with this well this year. Please reference inspection ID#: 2870841. I was contacted by Rick Engelbert with Irvine Run Resources on September 13, 2019 to report the release of an unknown volume of crude oil to the ground along Irvine Run. The spill was reported to have been contained and was actively being cleaned up. A site visit was arranged for September 16, 2019. Legree 30, (37-123-26419): I met with Rick Engelbert on site at approximately 10:30 on September 16, 2019 to conduct an site investigation. Rick indicated that the well was pumped on August 31, 2019. A strong odor was noticed near the well on September 1st. A small amount of oil was found to have been seeping from the ground surface at the base of a hill side some ways below the well location;(At a similar elevation as the spill that occurred in April but further down on Irvine Run). A syphon dam was constructed below the area that was seeping oil. Absorbent materials were applied periodically to absorb the oil. A boom and some straw bails were placed in the stream channel of Irvine Run as a precautionary measure. Very little oil was believed to have made it into the stream. A leak test was performed on the buried lead line system that services the well. A small hole was found in a portion of the line near the well. The excavation exposing the line was still open while I was on site. All of the contaminated soil appeared to have been removed from the hole. Similar to the excavation created to expose the last leak associated with this well, the soil that was excavated didn't seem to have much oil contamination. Heavy rain in the last week apparently caused the volume of oil draining from the seep to increase. It was at this point that Rick contacted me to report the spill. Approximately ten gallons of oil is reported to have been gather up. I noticed a slight emulsion on the surface of the water behind the syphon dam while I was on site. The spill appears to be getting managed appropriately at this point. The operator indicated the absorbent materials will continue to be changed as needed. It has been advised to the operator that recoverable waste materials, including the contaminated soil that was excavated around the leak, be collected and disposed of at a land fill. A receipt of disposal should be sent to the Warren District Office upon disposal. The clean up progress will continue to be monitored with future inspections.

Comments: At time of inspection, 56 degs. and sunny. There are (5) wells on this pad. They are the Jack 1H, 2H, WYO 3H, WYO 4H and the WYO 5H, all were in production. The (9x5) and the (13x9) annulus vents are plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe and tied into a 2" common pipe venting to the prod. tank with the exception of the 2H, which is a (2) string well and only has the (9x5) annulus venting to tank, the (20x9) annulus has an open top. All annulus vents are open and venting to production tank with the exception of the WYO 4H (20x13) annulus which has a Sentry valve venting to atmosphere. The cellars had water in them w/ no active bubbling observed during insp. An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 4/5/22) was turned on to check for gas at Sentry valve, cellars, at the well heads and left on during walk around pad and prod. equipment. Comments: A routine post-plugging inspection of the Spencer 1V well was conducted on January 25th, 2024. The well was plugged on 5/10/2023 and a Certificate of Well Plugging was submitted by the operator on June 8, 2023 certifying that plugging was complete. The document was reviewed for completeness and signed on August 23, 2023. At the time of inspection, the plugged well is buried below ground level. There was a thin layer of ice at surface above the well. A Remote Methane Leak Detector (RMLD) was used to check the ambient air above the well for methane. Violation ID: 8254342

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/30/2025
Comments: On October 30th, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of K Petroleum Inc's Mclvaine well site located in Somerset Township, Washington County following a voicemail and phone conversation where Operator Robert Inghram notified the Department of a 7-10 gallon release of crude oil from the production tank on to the ground within the tanks earthen dike. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead and a well posting fixed to the meter box on site, both of which had all required information posted on it. No active surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the wellhead, meter box, separator or fenced in production equipment on site.Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed a black tank to be within an earthen dike. The tank was observed to have orange/tan smudges and dried drip marks going down the side of it. What the Department believes may be peatsorb was observed on the ground at the base of the tank on top of puddles of fluid. This fluid had a possibly petroleum based odor and was observed to have an orange/tan film on top of it in some areas.The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the dike and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.826 mS and 0.904 mS in the release area, and 0.582 mS in berm of the dike. The Department also collected soil conductivity readings of 0.1705 mS and 0.1746 mS outside of where the peatsorb was observed. All of these readings were then compared to a background soil conductvitiy reading of 0.242 mS. The readings collected outside of the peatsorb are comparable to the background reading, subjugating that the release may be contained to the areas where peatsorb is observed. The readings within the fluid and in the side of the berm are elevated when compared to the background reading subjugating that the release has yet to be fully cleaned up.The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills. The Operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.While on site, the Department spoke with Operator Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's findings and of the aforementioned recommendations and requests. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for a 7-10 gallon release on to the ground from the production tank.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 986167
Permit API: 117-22124
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/23/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Johnson K 02-135 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 2/23/2023 at 0935 hours. The weather was 37 degrees with fog. A layer of snow covered the majority of the site today. An Act 9 sign is located at the site entrance.This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in to the DEP by Repsol on 2/16/2023. On 2/16/2023 at 0900 hours, a release of 18.7 gallons of produced water mixed with sand was released to the pad surface and containment from a sand trap. Repsol promptly called in the release to the DEP reporting hotline and began cleanup activities. A Repsol representative provided photos of the cleanup to me via email on 2/22/2023.During today's inspection, the impacted area was observed to have been excavated. All impacted material recovered was placed into containers for later disposal. No evidence of any portion of the release remaining was observed today. Pooled water in and around the impacted area was field measured for electrical conductivity ranging from 160 to 320us/cm. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #370057 is tied to this release within CTS.Based on the reported release of 18.7 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and containment, violations of 35 P.S. 691.402(b), 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), and 35 P.S. 6018.301 are cited against API #117-22124. However, due to Repsol's timely remediation of the reported release, these violations are considered immediately corrected at this time. Violations from a previous issue cited on 8/10/2022 and 9/2/2022 remain outstanding against API #117-22124. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8251224
Permit API: 129-26172
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Oklahoma Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/02/2025
Comments: On October 2 2025, the Department conducted a complaint inspection in regards to CTS 392648. This gas well is currently under an Order (Enf ID 442909). This inspection is not evaluating the operator's compliance with the Order and is being conducted in response to the aforementioned complaint.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the access road and well site appeared to be stabilized with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head and a well posting was present on a piece of the production equipment. There were no observed fluid leaks observed coming from the well head.Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed piping which ran to/from the production tank and the valve near the bottom of the tank, both of which appeared to be heavily corroded. It appeared a small about of fluid was seeping from the corroded portions of the piping onto the ground. The Department obtained a conductivity reading of the fluid on the pipe of 3.07mS. The Department obtained conductivity readings in the gravel below the corroded piping of 1.73ms and 0.87ms in an approximately 1 foot radius from the valve at the bottom of the production tank. These readings appear elevated in comparison to the Department's background conductivity reading of 0.22mS, indicating a release of production fluids has/is occurring.Prior to leaving the site, the Department attempted to contact the operator by calling the phone number on the well tag. The Department's call was sent to voicemail, and the Department was unable to leave a voicemail as the voicemail inbox was full.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed corroded production piping, as well as the observed release.

Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. There was 1 1/2'-2' of crude oil/water in the secondary containment at the time of initial inspection. A follow-up inspection on 12/26/2020 found that the liquid crude oil/water mix that was in the secondary containment had been removed however there was snow and ice partially covering the bottom of the containment. Between this inspection and the last inspection water has collected in the secondary containment from recent precipitation events. Crude oil contamination is evident on the surface of the water and and on the outside of the tanks. An empty 200 gallon tote is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/25/2024 to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEAR LAKE PROP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2024
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8206011
Permit API: 123-39874
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Columbus Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/25/2024
Comments: The Bittinger 4 disposal injection well is housed inside a shed and is plumbed directly to the Bear Lake Properties, LLC truck unloading area located approximately 1500 feet east of the Bittinger 4 well. Multiple pieces of liner have been placed on the floor of the shed around the well. At this time, standing fluid was visible on the liner. A conductivity meter was used to find that the fluid's conductivity was greater than 20,000 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The partially exposed dirt floor at the edge of the liner was found to have soils with conductivity greater than 1,000 uS/cm, with some measurements as high as 2,500 uS/cm being observed. The fluid originating from Bittinger 4 traveled southwest from the shed to the edge of the gravel well pad, as evident from the dead vegetation and exposed soils in this direction. The portion of the gravel pad downslope of the shed was noticeably wet despite recent lack of rain. Approximately three feet southwest of the shed, a conductivity reading of 4,000 uS/cm was observed a few inches below the surface of the gravel. Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Inspection Date: 3/23/2026
Comments: On March 23, 2026, the Department conducted Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Thompson/Bloniarz 1 plugged well located in Georges Township, Fayette County following IR 4111962, where the Department issued violations for failure to comply with a COA of the Department (for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of plugging of the well.) A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/07/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 12/07/2025 and a well site restoration report should be submitted to the Department by 2/05/2026.During IR 4111962, the Department observed a downed fence, an empty mailbox and a pile of compost filter sock (CFS) lying on the ground at the plugged well's graveled access road entrance. The Department also observed the plugged well site to be partial vegetated with puddles of stormwater and areas where CFS appeared to still be installed.On 2/4/26 (documented in IR 4136336), the Department attempted to conduct a CSE, however, due to snow cover, the Department was unable to assess the state of the plugged well site at that time.On 2/10/26, the Department spoke with and received an email from Operator Heather Empfield which stated "...the fence noted in your inspection report is the landowners. The damage you noted was not done during plugging operations, we do not have the right to touch it. We are working with this farmer and this field will be returned to agricultural use once the weather allows this. In your prior inspection the damage sock was removed because this was related to plugging operations.In the meantime, we are trying to get the Waiver to expedite closing this out."To date, the Department has yet to receive a WSRR resubmission with a Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver of Site Restoration.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the access road to this well site to still be graveled. A mailbox with the Post-Plugging Site Restoration Plan was still not observed to be on site.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the plugged well site to still be partial vegetated with stormwater puddles throughout. According to the 15 day response submitted by Blackhill Energy on June 22, 2022 the following actions have been taken:Vac trucks dispatched to suck remaining fluid from puddles and containment,Frac tanks associated with production fluids have been removed from site,Soils and rock have been screened and with elevated conductivity have been scraped and containerized for removal. Violations noted.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 2019-06-25
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 853700
Permit API: 047-25054
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-25
Comments: While drilling on 6/24, the operator encountered fresh water. Cement returns and drill cuttings ran down the location toward a stream. The operator dug two small pits to contain this water and solids in order to prevent discharge to the stream. Some of the dirt was pushed right to the edge of the stream. Rain overnight 6/24-25 allowed the pits to overflow and also caused sediment to run into the stream from the location and dirt piles. At the time of this inspection, the stream and pits were both colored with sediment, which could also be seen in a pond just downstream. Drilling will continue 6/26-27, after which the drilling contractor will empty the pits and backfill. It was suggested that they pump the water as far from the stream as possible and/or use a sediment filter bag to prevent any further discharge.

Comments: I spoke with Colter Dabney (Chief) on site. He said Universal started hydraulically fracturing 2 of the Marcellus Shale wells on December 9, 2019. Once a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEP's Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review, and attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed, the outstanding violations will be closed. I took electrical conductivity readings from 3 separate puddles on the pad surface with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. They ranged 0.60-0.80 mS/cm. Air temp 32F JLP
